document.title: Rumsfeld complains to George Tenet about the CIA
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Rumsfeld Lacked Intel on Who The Enemies Were Two Years After Afghanistan Invasion, Newly Published "Snowflakes" Show | National Security Archive
document.note: Rumsfeld complains to George Tenet about the CIA.

persons.name: George Tenet
persons.role: Director of Central Intelligence (CIA), recipient of the memo

mentions.quote: The next thing I see is you on television giving a speech at his gravesite.

persons.name: Donald Rumsfeld
persons.role: US Secretary of Defense, author of the memo

persons.name: Gen. Franks
persons.role: Commander, CENTCOM (CINCENT); named in handwritten marginalia

organizations.name: CIA
organizations.notes: Criticized for contradictory public-relations policy on disclosing its casualties in Afghanistan.

events.description: Rumsfeld sends a memo (snowflake) to George Tenet complaining about the CIA's contradictory public-relations policy on its casualties.
The first CIA person was killed; Tenet told others not to mention it, then spoke at his gravesite on TV.
A CIA person was wounded; CINCENT was told not to mention it, but CIA then publicized it repeatedly.
Rumsfeld sends memo to Tenet complaining about contradictory CIA public relations policies regarding casualties.
First CIA person killed; Tenet told DoD not to mention it, then spoke on television at his gravesite.
A CIA person was wounded; CINCENT was told not to mention it, but CIA later mentioned it repeatedly.

relationships.detail: Rumsfeld writes to Tenet, complaining of contradictory signals from the CIA.
relationships.quote: I am totally confused by the contradictory signals coming out of the agency.

relationships.detail: Tenet is addressed as the head of CIA policy.
relationships.quote: What in the world policy do you have?

relationships.detail: CINCENT was told by everyone not to mention the wounded CIA person.
relationships.quote: everyone told CINCENT not to mention it. So he didn't.

relationships.detail: Rumsfeld writes as Secretary of Defense; the memo is from his office, with the document's OSD reference.
CINCENT, the CENTCOM commander, was told by CIA not to mention the wounding of a CIA officer and complied.
relationships.quote: everyone told CINCENT not to mention it. So he didn’t.

relationships.detail: Handwritten note references Gen. Franks; CINCENT is CENTCOM's commander (Franks), inferred.
CIA told CENTCOM/CINCENT not to publicize a CIA officer's wounding; CIA later publicized it itself, creating friction.
relationships.quote: everyone told CINCENT not to mention it. So he didn’t. Now CIA is mentioning it repeatedly.

key_claims: Rumsfeld considered CIA public-relations policy on its Afghanistan casualties contradictory and confusing.
The CIA asked others not to mention the first CIA fatality, yet Tenet then spoke publicly at the gravesite.
CENTCOM withheld news of a wounded CIA officer at others' request, then the CIA publicized it itself.
